forms.footer: Note: Amazon asks these questions for the purpose of compliance with federal export control laws and regulations. Amazon will provide you immigration support and sponsorship where you and the role are eligible. Your answers to the immigration sponsorship question(s) will not automatically disqualify you from the job application process. forms.title: Voluntary Equal Employment Opportunity Self-Identification
forms.description:
As an Equal Opportunity Employer, Amazon does not use this information in its hiring decisions, so whether or not you choose to identify gender will not affect your application in any way.

Inclusion starts with knowing who we are as a workforce. By voluntarily and confidentially self-identifying, you help Amazon enhance policies and initiatives that support everyone. Your information is highly protected and used only in aggregate to strengthen our inclusivity efforts. Self-ID is a small action with a big impact. Be part of shaping a workplace that values and represents all Amazonians.

This privacy statement explains how we handle the personal data you provide when responding to self-identification questions. For details on terminology, data processing, or your privacy rights, please refer to Amazon's Employee Privacy Notice and the relevant regional addendums. If you’re outside the EU, contact your local HR team with any privacy questions. EU employees can contact their Data Protection Officer (DPO), if appointed, or email EU-staff-privacy@amazon.com.

questions.title: Do you identify as an Indigenous Person?
questions.description: The Employment Equity Act (Canada) defines Indigenous Persons as persons who are Indians, Inuit or Métis. This question does not seek to identify legal status or registration, only if you personally identify as an Indigenous Person.

questions.title: Do you identify as a person with a disability?
questions.description: The Employment Equity Act (Canada) defines a person with a disability as having a chronic, long-term or recurring physical, mental, sensory, psychiatric or learning impairment that may result in a disadvantage in employment. This includes people who have been accommodated in their workplace. This does not include short-term illness or injury.

questions.title: Do you identify as Black/Person of Colour or Visible Minority?
questions.description: The Employment Equity Act (Canada) defines members of Visible Minorities as a person, other than an indigenous person, who are non-Caucasian in race or non-white in colour.

forms.title: Voluntary Self-Identification of Military Status
forms.description:
At Amazon, we actively hire ex-military (serving or former member of your country's Armed Forces), serving members of your country’s Reserve Forces and military spouses in a wide variety of careers to allow them to apply their knowledge, skills, and leadership abilities to influence change, on behalf of our customers across the globe. Amazon operates a number of programs tailored to our military community. To help us track our progress with these initiatives and provide information on them to you we encourage you to disclose your status as ex-military, a member of the Reserve Forces of your country or a military spouse. Providing this information is completely voluntary and refusing to do so will not subject you to any adverse treatment.
